sections.html:
Conway is the Horry County seat, on the west bank of the Waccamaw River about 14 miles inland from the Atlantic and inside the Myrtle Beach metro area. Growth has been quick for a small city: 17,103 people in 2010, 24,849 in the 2020 census (a 45.3 percent jump), and an estimated 30,627 in 2025.

Downtown has older blocks, many near the Riverwalk, which is now a restaurant strip along the Waccamaw. Newer subdivisions lie farther out. The two kinds of housing sell differently, and homes within walking distance of the river are the ones owners point to first. Coastal Carolina University is also close, which is worth mentioning in a listing or when you talk to a cash buyer.

Water is the main risk for houses near the river, and Hurricane Florence in 2018 set the record. The river at Conway crested at 21.16 feet, more than three feet above the Hurricane Matthew crest. The county emergency plan uses these stages:

Flood levelRiver stage at ConwayWhat to expect
Minor11 feetRoads may be covered
Moderate12 feetBuildings usually begin to flood
Major14 to 16 feetLarge-scale evacuations may be needed

The watershed is large and flat, so rain upstream can take days to arrive and the river can stay high for a long stretch. After Florence, nearly 1,000 homes and businesses near the river flooded, and county officials later counted 361 damaged homes in Conway. Hurricanes Joaquin in 2015 and Matthew in 2016 damaged hundreds more across the county.

The city designs its riverfront parks to flood so that private property is spared, and it altered the electrical boxes in Riverfront Park so they can be pulled before water rises. For your own house, expect buyers to ask about flood history. Keep repair receipts, photos and any insurance claim papers in one folder. The NWS Hurricane Florence summary has the storm record.

sections.h2: Roads, storms and showing a house
sections.html: U.S. Routes 501 and 378 run through Conway. Florence closed more than 260 roads in Horry County, so buyers judge an address partly by whether it keeps a route open in a storm. A house on higher ground with a clear way out is easier to sell than one on a street that goes under. Summer rain is also hard on crawl spaces, drainage and roofs, so a dry crawl space and clean gutters help the house show better.

sections.h2: Property tax and the 4 percent rate
sections.html:
Horry County assesses property in Conway. A legal residence that the owner occupies is taxed at 4 percent of fair market value, and other property at 6 percent. The home plus up to five contiguous acres qualifies, as long as it is not rented more than 72 days in a calendar year. The owner has to apply before the first penalty date of the year eligibility is first claimed (Code section 12-43-220).

A buyer who rents the house out will not get the 4 percent rate, so an investor's bill can run higher than yours. The county Assessor's Office is at 1301 Second Avenue, Conway, SC 29526, open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., phone (843) 915-5040. Its Land Records application finds a parcel's PIN by address or owner name, and you need the PIN for the county Tax Estimator. More is on the Assessor page.

A deed that distributes an estate is spared the usual value affidavit under South Carolina Code section 12-24-70(D), so the paperwork is lighter than in an ordinary sale. A deed to a mortgagee in lieu of foreclosure is likewise exempt from the recording fee under section 12-24-40.

Heirs still have to agree, and the title has to be clear. Land records are held in the county, and a closing attorney will trace the chain of title before anyone signs. If heirs live in different states, start collecting signatures early, because a single missing signature can hold up the closing.

These cases come up often, and each affects which sale route makes sense:

  • A house flooded in a past storm that needs repairs before a bank will lend on it.
  • A rental with a tenant and no plan to fix it up.
  • An inherited house with several heirs spread across states.
  • A home with mortgage arrears and a deadline.

A flooded or heavily worn house is hard for a financed buyer, since the lender's appraiser may refuse to sign off until repairs are done. A cash buyer can take it as it stands. That can save you months of contractor bids and holding costs, though you should expect an offer that reflects the repairs.

If you are still deciding, call the city for the permit and utility details: it lists 14 departments, including Planning and Development, Public Utilities, Solid Waste and Construction Services. Ask Planning and Development about open permits, and Public Utilities about the final meter read, so you can close out accounts on the closing date.

sections.h2: From accepted offer to closing day
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, the buyer orders an inspection and a title search. With a loan there is also an appraisal, and in a flood-prone area the lender may require flood insurance before it funds. A cash purchase skips those lender steps and often closes faster.

The closing attorney prepares the deed and the settlement statement, pays off your mortgage and any unpaid taxes from the proceeds, and records the deed. Bring photo ID, your lender's contact details, keys, and any leases, repair records or insurance claim papers. Those papers answer the questions a buyer is most likely to ask about a Conway house.

If the house flooded, assemble a simple file before you list: dated photos, contractor invoices for the repair, the insurance claim outcome and your flood zone information. A buyer who sees the repair was done properly worries less, and a buyer who sees nothing assumes the worst. When you take a cash offer, the buyer will usually run their own numbers on those same records, so having them ready speeds the answer.

One more practical point: confirm your parcel's PIN early through the Land Records application. With the PIN you can pull the assessment, check the tax estimate and give a buyer or attorney exactly the right parcel from the first phone call. It also helps if a neighbor's lot is similar to yours, since mixing up parcels is an easy mistake.

faqs.q: How high did the Waccamaw River rise in Hurricane Florence?
faqs.a: It crested at a record 21.16 feet at Conway, more than three feet above the Hurricane Matthew crest. Nearly 1,000 homes and businesses near the river flooded.

faqs.q: What does the 4 percent rate mean on a Conway house?
faqs.a: It is the assessment ratio for an owner-occupied legal residence in South Carolina, against 6 percent for other property. The home cannot be rented more than 72 days a year, and you must apply before the first penalty date.

faqs.q: Where do I find a parcel's PIN in Horry County?
faqs.a: Use the county's Land Records application at horrycountysc.gov, which looks up a PIN by address or owner name. The Assessor's Office at (843) 915-5040 can also help.

faqs.q: Is a flooded Conway house hard to sell?
faqs.a: It can be, because buyers and lenders ask about flood history and insurance. Keep repair records and your flood zone details handy, and consider a cash offer if repairs are not an option.

faqs.q: Does Conway run its own city services?
faqs.a: Yes. The city lists 14 departments, including Planning and Development, Public Utilities, Solid Waste and Construction Services. Use them for permits and utility transfers when you sell.
